content: Do not take lisinopril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as lisinopril can harm the developing fetus. It is also used in combination with other drugs to manage heart failure. Additionally, lisinopril is prescribed to improve survival rates following a heart attack. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals in the body that cause blood vessels to constrict, allowing blood to flow more easily and enabling the heart to pump blood more effectively. Lisinopril is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once daily. To help you remember to take it, try to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take lisinopril exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than directed by your doctor. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting lisinopril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lisinopril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as enalapril, benazepril, captopril, fosinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking.g., indomethacin), diuretics, lithium, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have a history of heart or kidney disease, diabetes, lupus, scleroderma, or angioedema (a condition causing swelling and difficulty swallowing or breathing). Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking lisinopril. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes that contain potassium. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of lisinopril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Lisinopril may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: cough, dizziness, headache, fatigue, upset stomach, diarrhea, weakness, sneezing, runny nose, decreased sexual ability, or rash. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes; lightheadedness; fainting; or chest pain. If you experience any unusual problems while taking lisinopril, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store lisinopril in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness or fainting. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may also order lab tests to evaluate your body's reaction to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Lisinopril is sold under the brand names Prinivil® and Zestril®. Combination products containing lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide are marketed as Prinzide® and Zestoretic®.
